newsitem.title: GERMANY: Cohen meets Kohl, discusses Bosnia with generals.
newsitem.headline: Cohen meets Kohl, discusses Bosnia with generals.

text.p: German Chancellor Helmut Kohl urged U.S. Defence Secretary William Cohen on Wednesday to keep thousands of American troops in Germany and expressed optimism over improvement in NATO-Russia relations.

Cohen held what he called a "warm" 45-minute discussion with Kohl in Bonn midway through a four-day visit to Europe, then flew to Stuttgart where he met senior NATO military commanders on the peace-keeping mission on Bosnia.

Cohen told reporters flying with him from Bonn to Stuttgart that Kohl expressed satisfaction with progress on NATO enlargement and progress in relations with Russia and urged a continued presence of American forces in Germany where the United States now has about 75,000 troops.
Those forces have already been reduced from well over 200,000 during the Cold War.

"It was very good, very warm. We had a very cordial conversation," Cohen said, adding that Kohl expressed pleasure at Cohen's recent appointment as Defence Secretary because Cohen had long been interested in European affairs as a former U.S. senator.
"He thinks it's important that people be involved who have an understanding of U.S.-German relations certainly, but all of NATO," Cohen said.

"We discussed several key things. He feels it is very important that the United States maintain its presence in Germany and in Europe," the secretary said. "He knows that from time to time there are members (of the U.S. congress) who call for a reduction of U.S. forces, but he wanted me to know how important it was for the United States to remain engaged."
Cohen said Kohl also stressed the importance of the upcoming summit in Helsinki between Presidents Bill Clinton and Boris Yeltsin because of the need to move forward on Washington-Moscow relations.

"He (Kohl) felt that we are making progress as far as NATO enlargement and pursuing the NATO-Russia charter, but talked at some length about the importance of moving forward with President Yeltsin," said Cohen. "And so he was encouraging and somewhat optimistic about how things are unfolding."
Cohen said he and Kohl also discussed the dispute between the United States and France over continuing the American military command of NATO forces in southern Europe based in Naples.

Cohen said he had again insisted that the U.S. retain command of the area, but was now willing to review that decision "in four, five or six years" with the possibility of giving in to a French demand to give up the command to a European officer or share it with Europe.
"I think he (Kohl) fully understands that and is looking for creative ways in which we can hopefully still bring France into the NATO alliance," the secretary said.

Later, Cohen met in Stuttgart with U.S. Army Generals George Joulwan, the Supreme Allied Commander of NATO forces in Europe (SACEUR), and William Crouch, commander of NATO forces in Bosnia and of American forces in Europe.
He was forced by bad weather, which prevented helicopter flights, to cancel a planned visit to U.S. troops from the First Infantry Division.

The talks came midway through a trip by Cohen to Germany, Bosnia, Italy and NATO headquarters in Brussels before flying home on Friday. It is the secretary's first overseas trip since he was sworn in as the replacement for William Perry in late January.

Cohen told a news conference in Stuttgart that the discussion centred on Bosnia, but said in response to questions that the United States was closely watching the turmoil from civil unrest in Albania although the U.S. military had received no call to evacuate more than 1,000 Americans living there.
"...there are no military plans that have either been instituted or any need to call upon the U.S. military at this time," Cohen said.
Unrest in the former hardline communist country has escalated in recent days over the collapse of pyramid investment schemes.
Joulwan told reporters that the United States already had warships in the regis in contact with U.S. Ambassador Marisa Lino in Tirana.
